title: Fix covered call asymmetry: sell call spreads or fewer calls
summary: A covered call caps the upside while the downside stays linear, so losses can be much larger than gains. The speaker gives two fixes. Sell a call spread instead of a call, so you keep upside above the higher strike. Or sell fewer calls than you own, for example 4 calls on 500 shares, so part of the stock stays uncapped.

steps.caption: We own 500 shares at $100 and sell monthly calls.
A: the plain covered call. Upside stops at the strike, downside is linear: negative asymmetry.
B: also buy a higher call. Above that strike the position rises again with the stock.
The difference: B gives up a little premium to win back upside in a big rally.
Second fix: sell 4 calls on 500 shares. One lot stays uncapped. Set the long strike far away to compare.

takeaways: A covered call has capped upside and linear downside, so losses can exceed gains.
Selling a call spread instead of a call keeps upside above the higher strike.
Selling fewer calls than your share count, like 4 calls on 500 shares, also reduces the asymmetry.
caveats: The clip shows payoff charts that are not in the transcript; strikes here are illustrative.
Both fixes reduce premium income. The link-in-bio request is promotional.
